item.text: {"text":"Sampled listwise cross-entropy offers a plausible GRU4Rec objective alternative, but sampling corrections matter. [Correcting the LogQ Correction (RecSys 2025)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2507.09331) shows that conventional logQ correction mishandles the positive item: it is always included, whereas negatives are sampled. Its refined correction accounts for this distinction and introduces an uncertainty-dependent sample weight. Evidence comes from retrieval models, so transfer to GRU4Rec and HR@10 requires validation. [A 2024 sequential-recommendation study](https://arxiv.org/abs/2410.17276) compares uniform, popularity, in-batch, mixed and adaptive sampling; results vary with dataset popularity structure. Uniform sampling favors head items, while popularity sampling can improve balance at an overall accuracy cost.\n\nFalse-negative handling requires separate treatment from importance correction. [UFNRec](https://arxiv.org/abs/2208.04116), an earlier 2022 precursor, identifies suspected false negatives and uses teacher-generated soft labels; that teacher mechanism should not be imported into this constrained experiment. A compatible research hypothesis is one GRU4Rec trained with sampled listwise loss, an explicitly defined sampling distribution, and exclusion of known training positives. A uniform/adaptive mixture can retain sampling support, but deterministic top-hard selection cannot simply inherit a uniform logQ correction. Excluding observed positives reduces known collisions without identifying unobserved positives. Sampled softmax also does not directly optimize the tenth-rank boundary: harder negatives, temperature changes and sampling corrections remain hypotheses to assess using the fixed four-category macro validation HR@10."}
